casting-call: Pipeline Flow and Routable Paths

The whole system from a finished call to the review page, and every path a recording can take. Solid arrows are the main path. Amber dashed arrows are fallbacks and backups. Gold-outlined boxes are the files you keep. Since the 2026-10-08 version: the Zoom PodTrak P4next feeds OBS and keeps its own card as a backup, Deepgram does the transcribing, Meet captions put real names on the far side, and one pad press replaces the Stream Deck keys.

The paths in words

Recording. The P4next sends every channel to the Mac over one USB-C cable in Multi Track mode, and OBS's Call P4 scene records them as four tracks: a mix of your mic and computer audio built in OBS (Track 1), your mic (Track 2, P4next channel 1), computer audio, which is the far side (Track 3, channels 7-8), and the sound pads (Track 4, channels 9-10). No app audio capture is involved, so the Chrome capture that used to drop silently is out of the path. The P4next also writes every channel to its microSD card.

Getting the card off. In USB File Transfer mode the P4next is not the Mac's audio device, so ripcard copies only takes it has not pulled before (it keeps a .pulled list) and ejects the card as fast as it can. Then you choose which calls to keep and file the .mkv and its take into call_logs. That manual step is the filter: nothing processes a call you did not file, and nothing runs on a schedule.

ripa. Caption frame reading starts in the background with step 1 and runs alongside the rest. The card take is lined up with the video from the pad presses, which land on both, and fills any stretch where an OBS track went silent. Deepgram nova-3 transcribes both tracks at once, the far side diarized into speakers; a track whose request fails falls back to whisper on this Mac. A long far-side silence with no card to fill it gets its words from the captions. Then each Deepgram speaker is matched to the Meet caption name its words belong to: no roster, a clear winner only, and a second voice under one person's name becomes (second voice). Last, each pad press and PLAY-key mark becomes a [MARKER] marker line with a full-resolution frame. The run ends with a table of step times and the next command.

The report. /process-transcript in Claude Code writes the review page: what you were asked to do and what is owed to you first, then the summary, decisions and marked moments, with everything else behind Show more. It also writes a -summary.json for cross-call logs.

What changed, and why

OBS app audio capture is gone. On 2026-11-13 Chrome's capture stopped mid-call twice with no error in the OBS log. Recording the far side from the P4next's USB channel removes that dependency, and the card covers anything OBS still drops.

Deepgram does the transcribing. It takes seconds instead of minutes, and its diarization lets the far side split into people. Whisper stays as the fallback, and TRANSCRIBER=whisper keeps a run local.

Names come from the captions alone. The roster file is no longer needed; rips stays only for old recordings.

One marker. Pad A replaces the seven Stream Deck keys. What a press meant comes from the talk around it and the screen grab, which the report summarizes. Recordings from before 2026-11-14 still parse with their seven types.
